tools.name: get_started
tools.description: Start here. Returns what this server answers and which tool answers which question — find_analogs for a moment, get_topic_outcomes for a kind of recurring event, query_history for a condition, get_market_state for one moment, get_price_paths to draw them together — what the two rules mean for how yo

tools.name: find_analogs
tools.description: Find the past moments whose price shape most resembles a given one, each with the path that followed it. Reach for this when what you hold is a moment and what you want is other moments shaped like it. If what you hold is a condition you can state, use query_history; if it is a kind of recurring eve

tools.name: query_history
tools.description: Find every past moment a condition was true, newest first, each with what was knowable then and the path that followed. Reach for this when the condition can be stated; to search by the shape of the move instead, use find_analogs. A condition is one fact the bars can answer, written in words: the pr

tools.name: get_market_state
tools.description: Read what the market was at one moment and what happened after it: returns over 1h, 24h, 7d and 30d, the day's high, low and volume, how volatile it was against its own month, and the drawdown from the week's high. Use this for one moment's numbers; for the price path around a moment, or around seve

tools.name: get_price_paths
tools.description: Draw the price path around one or more moments, as percent from the close at each, so paths of different sizes can be laid over one another. Reach for it when you already hold the moments — from any of the searches — and want their paths side by side. For one moment's summary numbers, use get_market

tools.name: list_coverage
tools.description: List what this server can answer about: every asset with the name and aliases it answers to, where its data comes from, the first moment held and how far each scale reaches; the scales themselves; and the condition phrasings query_history reads. Call this before guessing a symbol, a scale, a date ra

tools.name: list_topics
tools.description: List the kinds of recurring event the data is indexed by — CPI releases, FOMC statements, rate cuts and holds, halvings, exchange failures — each with its slug and how many of them are held. Use this to find the slug for get_topic_outcomes; for a single dated event rather than a kind, use list_event

tools.name: get_topic_outcomes
tools.description: List every past event of one kind — every CPI release, every FOMC statement — each with what was knowable at that moment and the path that followed it. This is the tool for 'what happened the last N times this happened'. Reach for it when what you hold is a kind of event rather than a moment or a co

tools.name: list_events
tools.description: List dated events the data is indexed by — CPI releases, FOMC statements, options expiries — each with the moment it became known, the source it is taken from and the topics it belongs to. Use this to find or date a single event; for every event of a kind together with what followed each, use get_to

tools.name: compare_assets
tools.description: Read what every asset was doing at the same moment, side by side: the close, the day and three-day returns, the shape of the move before it and the path after, for each one. Reach for it when the question is about the surroundings of a moment rather than the one asset — what the dollar, the yields a

tools.name: get_bars
tools.description: Get the bars themselves — open, high, low, close and volume at a fixed step — for a stretch of time. Reach for it when the tools above do not shape the data the way you need it: your own measure, your own chart, a window none of them draw. For a moment read against its own history, use get_market_st
